key_insight: Finite-depth constrained QAOA is limited not just by feasibility, but by which feasible states are actually reachable by a specific shallow circuit and mixer schedule.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical diagnostic for designing resource-bounded QAOA circuits, helping engineers judge whether added depth or a different mixer is likely to improve objective quality rather than only expand feasible support.
method: Define the finite-depth accessible set R_p(M,x0) for a given feasible start state, mixer schedule, and circuit depth.
Use R_p to form a parameter-independent quality ceiling f_R* and a normalized reachable-quality score Q_R.
Compare structural diagnostics against shallow QAOA performance on constrained portfolio optimization and synthetic block-constrained quadratic problems.
evidence_signal: Across 207 favorable-tail CVaR QAOA configurations, Q_R had the strongest association with realized shallow-QAOA performance, with Pearson correlation 0.7003 and Spearman correlation 0.8057.
watch_item: R_p is a circuit- and schedule-specific upper bound, so its usefulness depends on accurate modeling of the compiled mixer/phase-separator implementation and may change with different hardware or compilation constraints.
paper_title: Beyond Feasibility: Finite-Depth Accessibility in Constrained QAOA
